name: Manjimup

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot, Sémillon and Cabernet Franc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Pinot Gris is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

soil.rock: Clay holds water well but drains poorly. It stays cool, which slows ripening and keeps acidity up.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
